outcome: Reproduction (e.g., number of ovarian cysts, first corpus luteum determination process)
cohort: The study involved 40 biparous cows (3 years old - second calving) with lameness associated with interdigital dermatitis from prepartum day 30 to postpartum day 60 (study group) and 40 biparous cows (3 years old) without lameness symptoms during the same period (control group).
finding: Wohlfahrtiimonas chitiniclastica bacteria were isolated for the first time in microbiological samples collected from cows with interdigital dermatitis, contributing to the understanding of the disease's etiology, and cows with interdigital dermatitis showed differences in postpartum beta-hydroxybutyric acid levels, weight loss, number of ovarian cysts, milk production, and first corpus luteum determination process compared to healthy cows.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference between cows with and without interdigital dermatitis in terms of reproductive parameters, including mode of delivery, litter viability, litter weight, expulsion of membranes, and presence of acute puerperal metritis during birth.
